test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

An educated lady __makes a better mother__ than an uneducated one.
solution:
The correct answer is- 'No substitution required.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct so no improvement is required.
 
• As we are talking in general and not about a current situation, so *option 2 *is incorrect.
 
• The **subject **is *singular *(**lady**) so it should be followed by a *singular verb *(**makes**). Hence option 3 is also incorrect.
 
• As we are **comparing **two kinds of person we need to use a *comparative degree *(**better**) and not a *superlative degree *(**best**).
 
• Thus *option 1 *is the correct answer.

And the correct sentence is: *An educated lady makes a better mother than an uneducated one.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's learn more about the **comparative **and **superlative degree**:

 
 
• When two *items *or *people *are **compared**, a **comparative degree **is used by putting ‘*er*’ to the **adjective **word followed by the word ‘than’.

 
 
• Example: *She is **smarter **than her sister.*
 
 
 
• *​*Similarly, when more than two things or people are compared, the **superlative degree **is used by putting ‘*est*’ to the **adjective **word.
 
 
• Example: *He is the **strongest **wrestler.*
